channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Uzbekistan: 133 of 238 SSPE-afflicted children unvaccinated against measles, says Health Ministry
item.description: Uzbekistan's Health Ministry reported that 133 out of 238 children diagnosed with Subacute Sclerosing Panencephalitis (SSPE) have not received the measles vaccine. Parents of these children gathered to request medication, medical aid, and financial support. SSPE is a fatal disease caused by the measles virus, leading to irreversible brain damage.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's economic growth reached 11 percent in eight months, says cabinet head
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's economy grew by 11 percent in the first eight months of the year, reaching 1.397 trillion soms, according to cabinet head Adylbek Kasymaliev. Investments in fixed capital increased by 61.2%, construction by 61%, industrial production by 8.8%, and agriculture by 6.4%.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan and Pakistan Sign Agreement to Boost Freight Transit
item.description: Kyrgyzstan and Pakistan have approved an agreement to expand transit trade, aiming to enhance Kyrgyzstan's integration into international transport corridors. The deal facilitates road, rail, and air transport to Pakistani seaports like Karachi, Qasim, and Gwadar, and includes infrastructure development.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Secures Up to $50 Million Grant for Green Energy Transition
item.description: Kyrgyzstan may receive up to $50 million in grant financing from the International Development Association for the iFIRST project, aimed at reducing greenhouse gas emissions and improving energy efficiency. The project seeks to establish a carbon financing system and support energy reforms.

item.title: Uzbek President Discusses Bilateral Relations and Cooperation with South Korea
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev gave an interview to 'The Korea Herald' discussing Uzbek-Korean relations, high-tech cooperation, investments, and regional partnerships. He noted a fivefold increase in trade and over $8 billion in Korean investments, highlighting future cooperation in AI, critical minerals, and smart cities.

item.title: NGMK transitions from digitalization to intelligent production with AI focus
item.description: The Navoi Mining and Metallurgical Combinat (NGMK) is advancing its digital transformation, moving towards intelligent production incorporating artificial intelligence. A seminar, co-organized with the Ministry of Mining and Geology, focused on practical applications of digital solutions and AI for forecasting and optimizing production processes.

item.title: Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov to visit South Korea for official talks and summit
item.description: Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov will make an official visit to South Korea from September 15-18 at the invitation of President Lee Jae Myung. He will attend the first Central Asia-Republic of Korea summit, participate in bilateral talks, and witness the signing of economic and investment agreements.

item.title: Uzbekistan proposes to calculate child support based on children's needs, not parental income
item.description: Uzbekistan is considering changing child support calculations to focus on children's needs rather than parental income. The proposal aims to ensure children receive adequate support by establishing a minimum consumer basket based on age. This would prevent parents from reducing payments by hiding income or taking low-paying jobs.

item.title: Uzbek President outlines five priority areas for economic cooperation with South Korea
item.description: During his visit, President Shavkat Mirziyoyev identified five priority areas for economic cooperation with South Korea. Prospective projects worth nearly $12 billion have been prepared. Additionally, a Strategic Partnership Program with Korea Eximbank valued at $8 billion was adopted.

item.title: Uzbekistan and South Korea Expand Cooperation in Critical Minerals and Technology
item.description: Uzbekistan's President Shavkat Mirziyoyev held talks with South Korean President Lee Jae-myung in Seoul, focusing on strengthening the special strategic partnership. Both leaders noted the growth in trade and investment, with over 700 joint ventures in Uzbekistan. Cooperation will expand in sectors like healthcare, industry, energy, and education.

item.title: Winners announced for energy sector sports competition "TES Cup"
item.description: Over 200 employees from thermal power plants across the country participated in the "TES Cup" sports competition, organized under the motto "One team, one goal, one victory!" Winners received diplomas, medals, and gifts.

item.title: Three children of Uzbek women imprisoned in Russia returned to Uzbekistan
item.description: The underage children of Uzbek women held in penal institutions in Russia's Mordovia and Samara regions have been returned to Uzbekistan. Consular officials facilitated the repatriation process, ensuring all legal procedures were completed.

item.title: Tajikistan and UNICEF discuss cooperation on environmental programs
item.description: Tajikistan's Committee for Environmental Protection met with the newly appointed UNICEF Representative to Tajikistan, Gabriella Akimova. They discussed cooperation on environmental protection programs aligned with the National Development Strategy until 2030 and priorities for the 2027 Joint Work Plan. Key areas include climate change, environmental safety, and ecological literacy for youth.

item.title: Uzbekistan's exports decrease by 3.6% in seven months, gold sales decline impacts total revenue
item.description: Uzbekistan's exports fell by 3.6% in the first seven months of the year, primarily due to a reduction in gold sales, which affected overall export revenues. Imports, however, saw an increase of approximately 18% during the same period. Detailed figures are available via the provided link.

item.title: South Korea and Central Asia Launch C5+1 Industrial Cooperation
item.description: South Korea and five Central Asian nations agreed to expand industrial cooperation, trade, and supply chains. Priority areas include trade development, industrial parks, strategic minerals like lithium, advanced technologies, and training specialists. The C5+1 format aims to be a platform for joint projects and economic ties.

item.title: Uzbek Citizen Injured in Drone Attack in Russia Repatriated
item.description: An Uzbek citizen severely injured in a drone attack in Nizhnekamsk, Russia, was brought back to Uzbekistan on September 13. The decision to repatriate was made after his condition stabilized and Russian doctors permitted evacuation. He is continuing treatment and rehabilitation in Uzbekistan.

item.title: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev Officially Welcomed in Seoul
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev received an official welcome ceremony at the South Korean presidential residence on September 14. President Mirziyoyev and his wife were greeted by President Yoon Suk Yeol and his wife. The ceremony included an honor guard and national anthems, followed by high-level talks.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Debt to China Revealed; Repayment Possible Now, Says Deputy Finance Minister
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's debt to China has been disclosed, with the Deputy Finance Minister stating it can be repaid immediately. However, he recommended a phased approach. The exact amount of the debt was not specified in the report.

item.title: Remote Sensing Center to Be Established in Dushanbe
item.description: Tajikistan's communications service and China's Great Wall Industry Corporation discussed cooperation in space technologies, including establishing a National Earth Remote Sensing Data Center in Dushanbe. The center aims to aid monitoring of natural and environmental processes.

item.title: Germany Offers 200 Construction Jobs for Uzbek Citizens
item.description: Uzbekistan's Migration Agency and Germany's RRG AG are recruiting construction specialists for 200 positions in Germany, offering a monthly salary of 2,000 euros. Applicants need relevant education and at least two years of experience. The employer covers visa and flight costs.

item.title: CSTO 'Border-2026' Exercises Begin in Kazakhstan with Tajik Military Participation
item.description: CSTO's 'Border-2026' exercises have commenced in Kazakhstan's Jetisu region, involving approximately 1,500 military personnel from Tajikistan, Russia, Kazakhstan, and Kyrgyzstan. The drills, focusing on combating illegal armed groups, will continue until September 18.

item.title: Tajikistan Extends Applicant Registration for Centralized Entrance Exams Until September 15
item.description: Tajikistan's National Testing Center has extended the third stage of applicant registration for centralized entrance exams to educational institutions until September 15 due to high demand. Registration points operate from 08:00 to 17:00.

item.title: Korean Company to Invest $100 Million in Uzbekistan Robot Factory
item.description: A Korean company plans to invest $100 million in building a robot manufacturing plant in Uzbekistan. Further joint projects in artificial intelligence, pharmaceuticals, and biotechnology are also anticipated.

item.title: Tajikistan Delegation Attends CIS Interpol Heads Meeting in Minsk
item.description: A delegation from Tajikistan's Ministry of Internal Affairs participated in a meeting of CIS Interpol bureau heads in Minsk, Belarus, from September 8-10. Discussions focused on strengthening international cooperation and combating transnational crime.

item.title: Kazakhstan to host AI & Digital Bridge 2026 forum with international tech leaders
item.description: Kazakhstan is fostering an open tech ecosystem and seeks international collaboration. The year 2026 is declared the Year of Digitalization and Artificial Intelligence, with AI MONTH running from September 23 to October 23. The central event, AI & Digital Bridge 2026, will take place in Astana from October 1-3, attracting global tech companies and investors.

item.title: Joint CSTO exercise 'Rubezh-2026' enters active phase in Kazakhstan
item.description: The active phase of the joint exercise 'Rubezh-2026' with the Collective Rapid Deployment Forces of the Central Asian region has begun at the 'Koktal' training ground in Kazakhstan. The exercise focuses on combating illegal armed groups invading CSTO member states' territory.

item.title: Uzbekistan Plans to Launch Two Waste-to-Energy Plants by Year-End
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to launch two waste-to-energy plants by the end of this year, with six such projects involving Chinese companies scheduled for 2026-2027. These projects, totaling $933 million, aim to process 3.6 million tons of waste annually and generate 1.6 billion kWh of electricity.

item.title: Russian and Tajik universities discuss expanding cooperation and promoting Russian language
item.description: Russian Deputy Minister of Science and Higher Education Konstantin Mogilevsky met with the rector of the Russian-Tajik (Slavic) University (RSU) in Dushanbe to discuss RSU's development. The meeting focused on enhancing cooperation with Russian universities, promoting the Russian language, and developing joint educational programs. Prospects for creating new programs and a Center for Professional Competencies were also considered.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Interior and Education Ministries enhance security measures for new school year
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Interior Ministry and Education Ministry are increasing security measures around educational institutions as the 2026-2027 academic year begins on September 15. Law enforcement will ensure student safety on roads, monitor traffic rules, and conduct preventive work. Drivers are urged to be cautious near schools, and parents are advised to discuss road safety with their children.

item.title: Lawyer seeks public help to cover damages for convicted Kyrgyz nephrologist
item.description: The lawyer for convicted Kyrgyz nephrologist Nasira Beyshebaeva is appealing for public assistance to help her pay over 2 million soms in damages awarded to a patient's mother. The doctor was sentenced to three years in prison. The lawyer stated the sum is unaffordable for the doctor and provided a bank account for donations.

item.title: Chubak aжы Jalilov Awarded 'People's Hero' Title Posthumously
item.description: Chubak aжы Jalilov has been posthumously awarded the highest title of 'People's Hero' of Kyrgyzstan. President Sadyr Japarov presented the award to his son, Abdullah Jalilov. The title recognizes his significant contribution to religious education and cultural traditions.

item.title: CIS Penitentiary Service Heads Convene in Kazan for Regular Meeting
item.description: The Council of Heads of Penitentiary Services of CIS member states held a regular meeting in Kazan on September 11, 2026. Representatives from Armenia, Belarus, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Russia, Tajikistan, and Uzbekistan attended. The meeting focused on strengthening stability and security within the CIS.

item.title: Uzbek President Proposes Building 'New Silk Road' with South Korea
item.description: In an article published in South Korea's The Chosun Daily, President Shavkat Mirziyoyev proposed establishing a 'New Silk Road' with South Korea. He analyzed historical ties, current strategic partnership, and future priorities, advocating for a 21st-century route through advanced industries and transport corridors.

item.title: Juma Odina: A courageous Tajik writer criticized Communist Party policies during the Soviet era
item.description: Juma Odina was a courageous Tajik writer who criticized Communist Party policies during the Soviet era. His novel 'Guzashti ayyom' faced backlash, leading to the burning of 14,000 copies. He was expelled from the Writers' Union and died in Dushanbe in 1982.

item.title: Uzbek electricians and concrete workers sought for jobs in Serbia with salaries up to 1500 euros
item.description: Serbia is offering 1,000 construction jobs for Uzbek citizens as part of preparations for the 2027 EXPO exhibition. Electricians can earn 1000-1500 euros monthly, while concrete workers will receive 700-1200 euros. Accommodation and food are provided.

item.title: ABank Receives High Rating from Independent Sustainable Fitch
item.description: ABank has received an 'Excellent' rating from the international rating agency Sustainable Fitch for its Green Financing Program, developed with support from the Global Green Growth Institute (GGGI). This independent assessment confirms the program's high compliance with international capital market principles and sustainable financing standards, paving the way for ABank's entry into the international green bond market.

item.title: Uzbekistan sees rise in court cases of violence against women
item.description: Uzbek courts processed 2,018 criminal cases related to violence and harassment against women in the first half of 2026, a 65.7% increase from the previous year. Of these, 1,624 individuals were convicted, and 2,146 women were identified as victims.

item.title: Saudi oil exports at risk as global supply could drop by 4%
item.description: Saudi oil exports face risks, with potential for a 4% drop in global supply, according to Reuters. The Tadawul All Share Index (TASI) fell 1.3% on September 13, marking its largest daily decline since early April.

item.title: Dushanbe to Host International Forum on Sustainable Tourism Development
item.description: Dushanbe will host the "Dushanbe International Tourism Exhibition – 2026" and the International Forum "City Integration in Realizing Sustainable Tourism Opportunities" from September 24-26. An organizing committee has been formed to manage these events, aimed at developing sustainable tourism, expanding inter-city cooperation, attracting investment, and promoting Tajikistan's tourism potential.

item.title: UK Ambassador: Uzbekistan's Independence Crucial for Britain, Discusses Reforms and Regional Security
item.description: As his mission concludes, UK Ambassador Timothy Smart reflects on his tenure in Uzbekistan (2023-2026). In his final interview, he discussed trade, investment, education, and security changes. Smart emphasized the importance of Uzbekistan's independence and territorial integrity for the UK and outlined prospects for cooperation with the Central Asian region.
